We expand near \(x=0\):

\[
e^{2x}-1 = 2x+2x^2+\frac{4}{3}x^3+O(x^4)
\]

So

\[
\frac{1}{x(e^{2x}-1)}
= \frac{1}{2x^2}\cdot \frac{1}{1+x+\frac{2}{3}x^2+O(x^3)}
\]

Using \(\frac{1}{1+u}=1-u+u^2+\cdots\),

\[
\frac{1}{x(e^{2x}-1)}
= \frac{1}{2x^2}\left(1-x+\frac{1}{3}x^2+O(x^3)\right)
= \frac{1}{2x^2}-\frac{1}{2x}+\frac{1}{6}+O(x)
\]

Also,

\[
\frac{x-1}{2x^2}=-\frac{1}{2x^2}+\frac{1}{2x}
\]

Adding,

\[
\left(-\frac{1}{2x^2}+\frac{1}{2x}\right)
+
\left(\frac{1}{2x^2}-\frac{1}{2x}+\frac{1}{6}+O(x)\right)
= \frac{1}{6}+O(x)
\]

Thus the limit is

\[
\frac{1}{6}
\]

Answer: H
